1.explanation: The StyledMeter styled component (StyledMeter.js) includes a global rule: `path { transition: all 0.3s; }`. This applies to every SVG path attribute—most notably the `d` attribute that defines the arc geometry. Chrome animates the shape change, causing the odd visual artifact. To fix, that CSS transition must be removed or restricted to only the intended stroke properties (e.g. `stroke-dashoffset`), so that the arc redraws cleanly without morphing its path data.
1.bug_scenario: When the Meter value changes on a circle‐type Meter in Chrome, the SVG path’s "d" attribute is being interpolated over a 300ms "transition: all" rule. Instead of redrawing the arc instantly or animating only the stroke properties, Chrome smoothly morphs the path geometry, producing a jagged, unintended animation. Firefox and Safari ignore that transition on path data, so they don’t show the issue.

2.explanation: StyledMeter is the single styled‐component that injects “path { transition: all 0.3s; }” into every path of the Meter. That CSS rule causes Chrome to interpolate the SVG path’s ‘d’ attribute on value changes, yielding the unwanted animation. Removing or scoping that transition (e.g. only animating stroke properties) in StyledMeter will prevent the path shape from morphing.
2.bug_scenario: The circle‐type Meter component applies a global “transition: all 0.3s” rule to every <path> in its SVG (via StyledMeter). In Chrome, updating the value re‐renders the SVG path’s “d” attribute and Chrome animates the morph between the old and new path outlines, producing a visible “weird” warped animation. Firefox and Safari do not animate “d” changes, so they just snap to the new shape.
